content_text: The Critics' Choice Movie Awards (in the original English: Critics' Choice Movie Awards), formerly known as the Broadcast Film Critics Association Award, have been presented annually since 1995 by the Broadcast Film Critics Association (BFCA) to honor the finest achievements in filmmaking. Written ballots are submitted for voting over a one-week period, after which the nominees are announced in December; the winners, chosen in a subsequent vote, are revealed at the annual ceremony held in January.

In addition, special trophies are presented at the discretion of the BFCA Board of Directors. Known for their credibility, they are among the most prestigious awards in American film and serve as a bellwether for the Oscars. The awards were originally titled simply the Critics' Choice Awards; however, in 2010, the word Movie was added to the name to distinguish them from the Critics' Choice Television Awards, which were first presented the following year by the newly created Broadcast Television Critics Association. The name Critics' Choice Awards officially refers to both sets of awards collectively.

content_text: From 2006 to 2009, the ceremony was held at the Santa Monica Civic Auditorium. From 2010 to 2012, it took place at the Hollywood Palladium. The event's television broadcast moved from VH1 to The CW in 2013, with the 19th ceremony airing live on January 16 of the following year from the Barker Hangar in Santa Monica, California.[7] In October 2014, it was announced that the Critics' Choice Movie Awards would be televised by A&E in 2015 and 2016.
